Because the chemical reaction that occurs to water when it freezes causes the formation of helium particles which in turn causes the ice to float over normal unfrozen water.

Fun fact: It doesn't always float. Like many chemical systems, you can get different phases (roughly meaning different kinds of atomic patterns) in ice. Some are actually denser than water. To generate these exotic kinds of ice, you usually need to really play around with the pressure and temperature of the environment - so you see more different kinds of ice on other planets and in outer space. (Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice#Phases).

That said, the dominant "normal" form on Earth is less dense than water and is sort of an anomaly, since most materials become denser as you freeze them. Water just happens to crystallize with a structure that has a low density at ambient temperatures/pressures.

The civil war and slavery issue is far more complex than most people know.

Some slaves were actually paid a salary (though they still worked by force, and their salaries were doubtlessly woefully small). In rare cases some slave owners let their slaves hunt for food (with guns,) in order to reduce operational overhead. Getting the slaves to feed themselves lowered the slave owners' expenses, and much of the calories a slave consumed from a self-caught wild boar or wild turkey went back into labor.

Most Americans don't know that New York was a slave state, and a huge number of the slaves brought from Africa were trafficked through New York. For a time New York, New Jersey, Delaware, and Maryland were all slave states. Also, during a long period of British rule these were slave colonies.

None of this is to say that slavery was morally defensible. What I'm saying is that it was complicated while it was happening, and now with the foggy hindsight of history mixed in with both current and 20th century politics - it is a huge complicated mess.

It is also complicated more since the question of slavery in the states was not in jeopardy as the Republican Party only aimed to prevent the spread of slavery in western territories, as abolition was still very unpopular. The notion is complicated further as the US supreme court ruled that congress had no authority to forbid slavery in territories in the Dred Scott ruling that nullified the Missouri compromise.
